name: Treasure State Eats: Montana
subtitle: Steakhouses, Drive-Ins & More
description:
Montana's restaurants, from a supper club on the prairie to a drive-in for a burger and a shake.

Treasure State Eats is a free guide to eating in Montana: 40 steakhouses and supper clubs and 7 drive-ins we checked by hand, the oldest places still open, plus 2,784 restaurants, cafés, bars and bakeries in 238 towns, from Billings and Missoula to Bozeman, the Flathead and the Hi-Line. No account, no ads.

MONTANA GUIDES
• Steakhouses & Supper Clubs: from prairie-town bars to the cities and the mountains.
• Drive-Ins: burgers and shakes, from small towns to the cities.
• Oldest Places: 8 restaurants open since 1960 or earlier, the M&M and the Oxford among them.
• James Beard Honors: 13 honored Montana restaurants.

FIND IT FAST
• Sort by distance, or browse the map by guide.
• Search by name, town, street or dish: "supper club", "steak billings", "drive-in".
• Filter by town or cuisine, or hide chains.
• Save places, and find hand-checked places from iPhone search (Spotlight).

LIVE DETAILS FROM APPLE MAPS
Tap "Ratings, hours & photos" on any place to open Apple Maps' own place card, with current hours, photos, ratings and directions.

HOW THE LISTS ARE BUILT
Every guide place was checked by hand in fall 2026 against Visit Montana's own listings (the state tourism office's), matched to an open listing at its address. The rest come from Overture Maps open data, kept by the reliability rule tested where cities publish official restaurant lists. Montana's county and city sanitarians inspect restaurants and publish no results as data; five counties post them on their own search pages, which their places link to, and elsewhere the app links the county health departments. Website links are checked too. Nothing is ranked by star ratings, and the app computes no grades. Newer restaurant data downloads from the Treasure State Eats website when there is some.

PRIVATE BY DESIGN
No account, no tracking, no ads. Your location, if you share it, only sorts lists on your device. Saved places stay on your device.

Places open and close, so check before you go. Spot a mistake? Email nick@eatsranked.com.

An independent app, not affiliated with any restaurant, chain or government agency (including the State of Montana, the Department of Commerce or Visit Montana, DPHHS, the Department of Revenue, or any county, city or tribe), or with the James Beard Foundation. James Beard Foundation and James Beard Award are trademarks of the James Beard Foundation. Place data from Overture Maps Foundation (CDLA Permissive 2.0) and others; sources and licenses are on the About tab.

reviewNotes:
1. Purpose and audience: Treasure State Eats is a free guide to restaurants in Montana (the U.S. state). Its focus is the state's own food: steakhouses and supper clubs, drive-ins and the oldest places still open, 55 places checked by hand in fall 2026 against the state tourism office's own listings, plus the James Beard honorees. It also lists 2,784 restaurants, cafés and bars in 238 towns from open map data. It is for residents and visitors deciding where to eat, with no ads, account or tracking.

2. How to use it (no login, no setup, no sample files needed):
- Home → Steakhouses & Supper Clubs (or Drive-Ins, James Beard Honors, Oldest Places, Near Me) → tap any place.
- On a place, tap "Ratings, hours & photos" to open Apple Maps' own place card through MapKit. Directions, Call and Website are below it; further down, a link opens the county's inspection search (or Montana's list of county health departments) in Safari.
- Search from the Home search box by name, town, street or dish ("supper club", "steak billings", "drive-in").
- The Map tab shows each guide as pins. "My location" and the Nearest sort use location only if allowed, on the device.
- The heart saves a place on the device (Saved tab). The About tab lists the sources, licenses and the independence statement.
- On iPad, a sidebar replaces the tabs; a place opens in the right-hand column.
- Location: if you're outside Montana (as App Review usually is), the map says so and stays on Montana, and distance sorting still works from where you are.
- "Treasure State Eats" is the Home Screen name of "Treasure State Eats: Montana".

3. External services and data:
- Apple MapKit: maps, local search to find a place's Apple Maps listing, and Apple's place card for live hours, photos and ratings.
- Core Location: optional, on-device only, for distance sorting.
- Data updates: at most once a day, the app checks the Treasure State Eats website (static files on GitHub Pages) for newer restaurant data and downloads it if there is some. The requests carry no identifiers or location.
- No backend, accounts, analytics, advertising, payments or AI services. The restaurant data is bundled in the app.
- Bundled data sources: Overture Maps Foundation open place data (CDLA Permissive 2.0 and others; license texts are in the app); James Beard Foundation honors (facts only); and our own research of public websites and Visit Montana's listings.
- The website with the privacy policy and support page is static and hosted on GitHub Pages: https://nickstrom5.github.io/montana-eats/

4. Regional differences: none. The content covers Montana; the app is offered in the United States and works the same everywhere.

5. Regulated or protected material: the app is not in a regulated industry and includes no protected third-party material. The data is open-licensed or public record, with attribution and licenses on the About tab. Ratings, hours and photos are shown only inside Apple's own place card through MapKit; the app stores no ratings or reviews. The app shows no inspection results and computes no grades. Every website link was checked before release, and adult venues are excluded. The app is independent and not affiliated with any restaurant, agency or award body.

Support: nick@eatsranked.com
